verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 36.17
verses.english: Linked Discourses 36.17

verses.pali: 2. Rahogatavagga
verses.english: 2. In Private

verses.pali: Paṭhamasambahulasutta
verses.english: With Several Mendicants (1st)

verses.pali: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “katamā nu kho, bhante, vedanā, katamo vedanāsamudayo, katamo vedanānirodho, katamā vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā?
verses.english: “Sir, what is feeling? What’s the origin of feeling? What’s the cessation of feeling? What’s the practice that leads to the cessation of feeling?

verses.pali: Ko vedanāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṁ nissaraṇan”ti?
verses.english: And what is feeling’s gratification, drawback, and escape?”

verses.pali: “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, vedanā—
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these three feelings:

verses.pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā—
verses.english: pleasant, painful, and neutral.

verses.pali: imā vuccanti, bhikkhave, vedanā.
verses.english: These are called feelings.

verses.pali: Phassasamudayā vedanāsamudayo;
verses.english: Feeling originates from contact.

verses.pali: phassanirodhā vedanānirodho.
verses.english: When contact ceases, feeling ceases.

verses.pali: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vedanānirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: The practice that leads to the cessation of feelings is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

verses.pali: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
verses.english: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

verses.pali: Yaṁ vedanaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, ayaṁ vedanāya assādo.
verses.english: The pleasure and happiness that arise from feeling: this is its gratification.

verses.pali: Yaṁ vedanā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṁ vedanāya ādīnavo.
verses.english: That feeling is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

verses.pali: Yo vedanāya chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṁ, idaṁ vedanāya nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: Removing and giving up desire and greed for feeling: this is its escape.

verses.pali: Atha kho pana, bhikkhave, mayā anupubbasaṅkhārānaṁ nirodho akkhāto.
verses.english: But I have also explained the progressive cessation of activities. …

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa vācā niruddhā hoti …pe…
verses.english: For someone who has attained the first absorption, speech has ceased. …

verses.pali: khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno rāgo niruddho hoti, doso niruddho hoti, moho niruddho hoti.
verses.english: For a mendicant who has ended the defilements, greed, hate, and delusion have ceased.

verses.pali: Atha kho pana, bhikkhave, mayā anupubbasaṅkhārānaṁ vūpasamo akkhāto.
verses.english: And I have also explained the progressive settling of activities.

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa vācā vūpasantā hoti …pe…
verses.english: For someone who has attained the first absorption, speech has stilled. …

verses.pali: khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno rāgo vūpasanto hoti, doso vūpasanto hoti, moho vūpasanto hoti.
verses.english: For a mendicant who has ended the defilements, greed, hate, and delusion have stilled.

verses.pali: Chayimā, bhikkhave, passaddhiyo.
verses.english: There are these six levels of tranquility.

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa vācā paṭippassaddhā hoti.
verses.english: For someone who has attained the first absorption, speech has been tranquilized.

verses.pali: Dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā paṭippassaddhā honti.
verses.english: For someone who has attained the second absorption, the placing of the mind and keeping it connected have been tranquilized.

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa pīti paṭippassaddhā hoti.
verses.english: For someone who has attained the third absorption, rapture has been tranquilized.

verses.pali: Catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa assāsapassāsā paṭippassaddhā honti.
verses.english: For someone who has attained the fourth absorption, breathing has been tranquilized.

verses.pali: Saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca paṭippassaddhā honti.
verses.english: For someone who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have been tranquilized.

verses.pali: Khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno rāgo paṭippassaddho hoti, doso paṭippassaddho hoti, moho paṭippassaddho hotī”ti.
verses.english: For a mendicant who has ended the defilements, greed, hate, and delusion have been tranquilized.”

verses.pali: Sattamaṁ.
